hints.basics: Start with your name and how employers can reach you. The headline is a short line about who you are, such as your job title.
hints.summary: Write 2-3 sentences about who you are, what you're good at and what you're looking for. It's the first thing a recruiter reads.
hints.experience: Add your jobs, most recent first. Aim for 2-4 bullet points about what you achieved, ideally with numbers. Click a job to edit it.
hints.education: Add your education, most recent first. Degree and school are usually enough.
hints.skills: Type one skill at a time and press Enter. Pick the ones most relevant to the job you're applying for.
hints.languages: Pick a language and your level. Include your native language and any languages you can use at work.
hints.extras: Optional. Add certifications, a driving licence, volunteering or anything else that strengthens your CV.
hints.template: Pick the design you like best. Your content moves over automatically and you can switch at any time.
hints.visibility: Optional. Choose which sections to show, how long the CV may be and which language the headings use.

help.title: About Free Resume
help.intro: A simple, free, and fast way to create a professional CV.
help.step1: Upload your LinkedIn PDF (or start from scratch)
help.step2: Edit content, choose a template, and customize
help.downloadText: Click the "Download PDF" button in the top menu. Your CV is generated directly in the browser.
help.dataText: Your CV only lives in your browser and disappears when you close the tab. To continue later, save a CV file or turn on "Remember my CV" under Settings. If you accept analytics cookies, anonymous usage data is sent to Google Analytics. No personal information is shared.
help.footer: Free Resume is free and open source.

consent.message: We use cookies for anonymous analytics to improve this service. No personal data is collected.

checklist.title: Before you download
checklist.description: A few things could make your CV stronger. Fix them or download anyway.

start.title: Turn your LinkedIn profile into a polished CV in a minute
start.trust: Free, no account needed. Your PDF is read in your browser and never uploaded to a server.
start.mobileNotice: LinkedIn can only save your profile as a PDF in a desktop browser, not in the mobile app. If the file is already on your phone, choose it below.
start.step1Title: Open your LinkedIn profile on a computer
start.step2Title: Click Resources and choose Save to PDF
start.step2Hint: The button is below your name. On some accounts it's called More.
start.trouble1: Look for More instead of Resources.
start.trouble2: Use LinkedIn in a browser on a computer, not in the app.
start.trouble3: If the button is missing, temporarily switching LinkedIn's language to English can help.
start.trouble4: If it still doesn't work, use Start from scratch above the guide.
start.dropTitleTouch: Tap to choose your LinkedIn PDF
start.welcomeBack: Welcome back! Drag in the PDF you just saved.
start.dropHint: The file is usually called Profile.pdf and is in your Downloads folder. PDF only, max 10 MB.
start.dropOverlay: Drop the file to create your CV
start.pdfError: This PDF couldn't be read as a LinkedIn profile. Save it with Resources and Save to PDF on your profile (step 2) and try again.
start.sampleCaption: What your CV can look like
start.howToTitle: How to get your LinkedIn PDF
start.howToHint: Takes about a minute. LinkedIn saves your whole profile as one PDF file.
